newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower in sluggish trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower in sluggish month-end dealings that saw blue chip Banco Ganadero drop on profit-taking a day after it reported lower-than- expected third quarter earnings.

Bogota's IBB index fell 0.44 percent to 873.41 on a trading volume of 1.99 billion pesos. Medellin's IBOMED general price index dropped 0.22 percent, meanwhile, ending at 13,537.53 on an anemic volume of just 182.9 million pesos.
Losers in Bogota were led by heavily traded Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary shares fell 1.09 percent to end at 270 pesos per share.

The bank, Colombia's largest in terms of assets, reported late Tuesday that its net profit for the third quarter totalled 14.7 billion pesos, down 23 percent from 19.1 billion in the third quarter of 1995.

Other losers included Banco de Colombia, which fell 0.45 percent amid what brokers described as a continuing lack of follow-up information on plans announced last week to forge a strategic partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispano.
Brewer Bavaria SA was also hit by profit-taking, falling 0.26 percent to end at 4,089 pesos per share.

Thinly-traded Banco Anglo Colombiano was among the day's few winners in Bogot, jumping 9.17 percent to close at 59.50 pesos per share on what brokers described as a large cross-trade involving more than 507 million pesos in shares.

In Medelln, movers included Banco de Bogot, which fell 0.81 percent to close at 6,100 pesos per share. Cadenalco, Colombia's largest retailer, also ended lower, dropping 1.41 percent to 907 pesos a share.
Banco de Colombia managed to eke out a 0.22 percent gain, however, ending at 441 pesos per share.
